chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Shah narrated that Abu Hamid quoted on the authority of Abu Yazid Ahmad ibn Khalid al-Khalidy, who said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Salih al-Tamimy narrated to us, from his father, who said: Muhammad ibn Hatam al-Qattan to us, from Hammad ibn Amr, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) who said in his will to him:

O Ali! Indeed the Blessed the Sublime God has granted me seven characteristics similar to you. You will be the first one whom the grave will push out of the ground (on the Resurrection Day) along with me. You will be the first one to stop on the Bridge with me. You will be the first one to be dressed when they dress and are brought back to life when they are brought back to life. You will be the first one to reside with me in the highest Heaven. You will be the first one to drink the sealed nectar drink of Paradise with me which is sealed by musk.

key_terms.الصِّرَاط: The Bridge (Sirat) over Hell on Judgment Day
key_terms.عَلِيِّينَ: The highest Heaven (a specific level of Paradise)

ai.seo_question: What are the seven characteristics granted to Ali ibn Abi Talib according to this hadith from al-Khisal?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* via the prominent chain of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, this hadith underscores the unique ontological status of Ali ibn Abi Talib as the Prophet’s spiritual successor. It emphasizes his precedence in eschatological milestones—such as rising from the grave and crossing the Sirat—highlighting the Shia belief in his exclusive closeness to the Prophet in both this world and the Hereafter.
